MEMORANDUM

TO: Members of the Board of Directors, Halden & Marchetti Industrial Supply Corporation
FROM: Office of the Corporate Secretary, Loretta Kwan
DATE: March 4, 2025
RE: Briefing Materials for Quarterly Board Meeting, March 12, 2025

This memorandum is intended to provide members of the Board with background information and context in advance of the upcoming quarterly meeting scheduled for Wednesday, March 12, 2025, beginning at 9:00 a.m. in the Fourth Floor Conference Room at the corporate headquarters on Delacroix Avenue. As in prior quarters, materials referenced herein have been distributed separately through the secure board portal, and directors are encouraged to review the attached appendices prior to the meeting to allow for a more efficient discussion during the allotted time.

The first substantive item on the agenda will be the presentation of the fiscal fourth-quarter financial results by Chief Financial Officer Desmond Achebe. Preliminary figures indicate that consolidated revenue for the quarter came in at approximately $42.6 million, representing a modest increase of 3.1 percent over the same period last year. This growth was driven primarily by continued demand in the industrial fastener and hardware distribution segment, which has benefited from stabilized input costs following the supply chain disruptions experienced in prior fiscal years. Operating margins remained largely consistent with prior guidance, though Mr. Achebe has indicated he will address a slight uptick in logistics expenditures attributable to increased fuel surcharges from the company's primary freight partners. The Board should anticipate a detailed variance analysis comparing actual results to the budget approved in September, with particular attention paid to the Midwest distribution center, which underperformed relative to projections during the months of December and January.

Following the financial presentation, the Board will receive an operational update from Chief Operating Officer Priscilla Vantongeren regarding the ongoing warehouse modernization initiative at the Council Bluffs facility. This project, which was approved by the Board in the June meeting of last year, remains on schedule for completion in the third quarter of this fiscal year, with capital expenditures tracking within approximately two percent of the originally approved budget. Ms. Vantongeren will provide an update on the installation of the new automated inventory management system, including a brief overview of the vendor selection process that concluded with the engagement of Bramwell Systems Group as the primary technology integrator. The Board previously requested periodic updates on this matter given the scale of the investment, and this presentation is intended to satisfy that request for the current quarter.

The Board will also consider a proposal from the Human Resources Committee, to be presented by Committee Chair Nathaniel Osgood, regarding proposed revisions to the company's employee benefits package for the upcoming enrollment period. The proposal, developed in consultation with the company's benefits broker, Ashcombe Partners, would introduce an additional tier of health insurance coverage options intended to address employee feedback collected through the annual satisfaction survey conducted in October. The Committee's recommendation includes a modest increase in the company's contribution toward premium costs, which has been modeled against projected enrollment figures and is not expected to materially affect the fiscal year budget beyond the reserves already allocated for benefits administration. Directors with questions regarding the actuarial assumptions underlying this proposal are encouraged to direct them to Mr. Osgood in advance of the meeting, as the supporting documentation from Ashcombe Partners has been included in Appendix C of the board materials.

A further item for discussion will concern the renewal of the company's contract with its external auditor, Fennimore & Clark LLP, whose current engagement is set to expire at the conclusion of this fiscal year. The Audit Committee, chaired by Board member Regina Costanzo, has completed its annual review of the auditor's performance and independence and will recommend renewal of the engagement for an additional three-year term, subject to the customary annual reaffirmation process. Ms. Costanzo will summarize the Committee's findings, which included a review of audit fees relative to comparable engagements at similarly sized companies within the industrial distribution sector. No material concerns were identified during this review, and the Committee's written report has been circulated separately for the Board's reference.

The meeting will also include a brief update from General Counsel Marcus Delacroix-Whitfield regarding the status of several routine commercial matters, including the renewal of the company's lease for the Tulsa regional office and an update on the pending trademark registration for the company's newly introduced product line of corrosion-resistant fastening systems. Mr. Delacroix-Whitfield does not anticipate that either matter will require formal Board action at this time, though he will remain available to answer questions.

Section 7: Remote Work and Flexible Scheduling Policy

Meridian Analytics Group recognizes that the modern workplace has evolved to accommodate a variety of working arrangements that support both organizational needs and employee well-being. This policy outlines the guidelines and expectations governing remote work, hybrid schedules, and flexible hours for all eligible employees across the company's divisions, including the Client Services team, the Data Insights unit, and the Operations department. This policy applies to all full-time and part-time employees who have completed their initial ninety-day introductory period, unless otherwise specified by their direct supervisor or department head.

Eligibility for remote or hybrid work arrangements is determined on a role-by-role basis, taking into account the nature of the position, the employee's performance history, and the operational requirements of the team. Employees interested in pursuing a flexible work arrangement should submit a Flexible Work Request Form to their supervisor at least fourteen business days in advance of the desired start date. Supervisors are expected to review these requests in consultation with the Human Resources department, currently led by Regional HR Director Pamela Osei, and to provide a written response within ten business days of submission. Approval is not guaranteed and may be revoked at management's discretion if performance concerns arise or if business needs change.

Employees who are approved for remote work are expected to maintain a dedicated workspace that is free from excessive noise and distraction during core business hours. Core business hours at Meridian Analytics Group are defined as 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. local time, during which all employees, regardless of work location, are expected to be reachable via company email, instant messaging platforms, or telephone. Outside of these core hours, employees working flexible schedules may arrange their remaining working hours in a manner that suits their personal circumstances, provided that they complete their required weekly hours and attend all scheduled meetings, including the weekly Monday morning departmental sync and any client-facing calls scheduled by their supervisor.

All remote employees are required to have access to a stable internet connection with a minimum download speed of 25 megabits per second. The company's Information Technology department, overseen by IT Manager Colin Fitzhugh, will provide a standard equipment package to eligible remote employees, which includes a laptop computer, a docking station, and a headset. Employees are responsible for the security of this equipment and must report any loss, theft, or damage to the IT Help Desk within twenty-four hours of discovery. Requests for additional equipment, such as external monitors or ergonomic keyboards, may be submitted through the internal Equipment Request portal and will be evaluated based on budgetary considerations and role requirements.

Employees working remotely are expected to adhere to the same standards of professionalism, productivity, and conduct that apply to employees working from one of the company's physical office locations, including the corporate headquarters in Danforth Crossing and the satellite office in Ridgemont Park. This includes compliance with all existing company policies regarding data privacy, confidentiality, and the appropriate use of company technology resources. Employees handling sensitive client information, such as members of the team supporting the Halbrook Logistics account or the Kettleman Foundation engagement, must ensure that all work is conducted through approved, encrypted channels and that physical documents containing confidential information are stored securely and not left unattended in shared or public spaces.

Performance expectations for remote and hybrid employees remain consistent with those for in-office staff. Supervisors will continue to conduct regular one-on-one check-ins, typically on a biweekly basis, to discuss ongoing projects, address any challenges related to remote work, and provide feedback on performance. Employees are reminded that participation in the company's annual performance review cycle, which is administered each spring under the coordination of the Talent Development team, is required regardless of work location. Remote employees should ensure they have access to a quiet, private space for these review discussions to maintain confidentiality.

In situations where an employee's role requires periodic in-person attendance, such as team-building events, client presentations, or department-wide meetings, employees on remote or hybrid arrangements will be given a minimum of two weeks' notice, except in cases of urgent business need. Reasonable travel expenses incurred for such required in-person attendance will be reimbursed in accordance with the company's Travel and Expense Policy, as outlined in Section 12 of this handbook. Employees who reside more than one hundred miles from their assigned office location should discuss travel logistics with their supervisor in advance to ensure adequate planning time.

Meridian Analytics Group reserves the right to modify, suspend, or terminate any employee's remote or flexible work arrangement at any time, with or without cause, based on business needs or performance considerations. Employees who are found to be in violation of this policy, including failure to remain reachable during core business hours, misuse of company equipment, or noncompliance with data security protocols, may be subject to corrective action up to and including termination of the flexible work arrangement and, in serious cases, termination of employment. Any questions regarding this policy, including questions about eligibility, equipment requests, or scheduling exceptions, should be directed to the Human Resources department or to an employee's immediate supervisor. This policy will be reviewed annually by the Human Resources and Operations leadership teams and is subject to change as the company's operational needs evolve. Employees will be notified in writing of any material changes to this policy prior to their implementation, and continued employment following such notification constitutes acceptance of the updated terms.

## Project: Meridian Ledger Reconciliation Module (MLRM-2.3)

### Document Control Number: TSD-2024-0417

### Prepared by: Systems Architecture Group, Corvid Analytics Solutions

### 1. Purpose and Scope

This document defines the technical requirements, architecture, and implementation parameters for the Meridian Ledger Reconciliation Module, version 2.3 (hereafter "MLRM" or "the Module"). The Module is designed to automate the reconciliation of transactional records between the Corvid Analytics Solutions internal general ledger system, known internally as Halden Ledger Suite, and third-party vendor invoicing platforms utilized by regional distribution partners. This specification is intended for use by the Development Team, Quality Assurance personnel, and integration partners who require a comprehensive understanding of the Module's functional boundaries, data handling procedures, and interface requirements. This document does not cover deployment scheduling, licensing terms, or personnel training materials, which are addressed under separate documentation issued by the Program Management Office.

### 2. Background

The Meridian Ledger Reconciliation Module was commissioned following an internal audit conducted in the third quarter of the prior fiscal year, which identified recurring discrepancies between reported vendor invoices and recorded disbursements within three regional offices, namely the Brindlewood, Fenmark, and Castellane branches. The audit, led by Internal Controls Director Margaret Oswin, recommended the development of an automated reconciliation tool to reduce manual reconciliation labor and to minimize the incidence of unmatched or duplicate entries. This specification builds upon the findings documented in Audit Report AR-2023-119 and incorporates feedback gathered during stakeholder interviews conducted with regional finance leads Thomas Everley and Priya Ramanathan.

### 3. System Overview

MLRM operates as a middleware component situated between the Halden Ledger Suite database and external vendor data feeds. The Module ingests transaction records in comma-separated value format, XML format, or via direct API calls where supported by the vendor platform. Upon ingestion, records are normalized into a standardized internal schema referred to as the Unified Transaction Record (UTR). The UTR format includes fields for transaction identifier, vendor identifier, transaction date, amount, currency code, and a reconciliation status flag. Once normalized, records are passed through the Matching Engine, which applies a series of configurable rules to identify corresponding entries between the internal ledger and the external vendor feed.

The Matching Engine supports both exact-match and fuzzy-match reconciliation modes. Exact-match mode requires identical values across transaction identifier, amount, and date fields. Fuzzy-match mode, intended for use where vendor systems introduce minor formatting inconsistencies, applies configurable tolerance thresholds for date variance (default setting of plus or minus two business days) and amount variance (default setting of plus or minus one percent). Records that fail to match under either mode are routed to the Exception Queue for manual review by designated reconciliation analysts.

### 4. Functional Requirements

The Module shall support batch processing of transaction volumes up to two hundred fifty thousand records per reconciliation cycle without degradation of processing time beyond the established service level target of four hours per cycle. The Module shall maintain a complete audit trail of all matching decisions, including timestamps, applied rule sets, and the identity of any analyst who manually overrides an automated match determination. All audit trail data shall be retained for a minimum period of seven years in accordance with corporate records retention policy RP-4402.

The Module shall provide a configuration interface allowing authorized administrators to adjust matching tolerance thresholds without requiring a code deployment. This interface shall be accessible only to users holding the Reconciliation Administrator role within the Corvid Analytics Solutions identity management system, and all configuration changes shall be logged with the administrator's user identifier and the timestamp of the change.

The Module shall generate a daily summary report detailing the total number of records processed, the number of successful matches under exact-match mode, the number of successful matches under fuzzy-match mode, and the number of records routed to the Exception Queue. This report shall be distributed automatically via internal email to the distribution list maintained by the Finance Operations team, with Derek Halloway serving as the current list owner.

### 5. Non-Functional Requirements

The Module shall be deployed within the existing Corvid Analytics Solutions data center infrastructure and shall not require provisioning of additional physical hardware beyond the two application servers already allocated under infrastructure ticket INF-8834. The Module shall maintain an uptime target of 99.5 percent measured on a monthly basis, excluding scheduled maintenance windows communicated at least seventy-two hours in advance.

Data at rest within the Module's staging database shall be encrypted using AES-256 encryption, consistent with corporate data security policy DS-1120. Data in transit between the Module and vendor platforms shall be secured using TLS 1.2 or higher. Access to the Module's administrative functions shall require multi-factor authentication in accordance with existing corporate access control standards.

### 6. Interfaces

The Module interfaces with the Halden Ledger Suite via a dedicated read-write database connection managed through the existing Enterprise Service Bus, maintained by the Infrastructure Services group under the direction of Networking Lead Samuel Bricktoft. External vendor interfaces vary by partner and are documented individually in Appendix C of the associated integration guide, maintained separately from this specification. Any changes to vendor-side data formats shall be communicated to the Development Team no fewer than fourteen calendar days prior to implementation to allow for adequate testing.

This memorandum summarizes the renewal review conducted for the vendor agreement between Halden Ridge Logistics Corporation and Braxton-Miller Supply Solutions, covering the period of the upcoming contract term beginning March 1 and extending through the following twenty-four months. The review was completed by the Procurement Standards Committee in coordination with the Vendor Relations office, with input solicited from the Operations and Finance departments given the scope of services provided under the current agreement. The purpose of this document is to consolidate findings from the renewal assessment, outline the negotiated terms, and provide a record for internal reference should questions arise during the audit cycle scheduled for the third quarter.

Braxton-Miller Supply Solutions has served as the primary vendor for warehouse packaging materials and related consumables since the original agreement was executed under the tenure of former Procurement Director Elaine Ostrowski. The relationship has been characterized by consistent delivery performance, with only minor deviations noted in the quarterly service logs, most of which were attributed to regional transportation disruptions rather than vendor error. Over the past contract cycle, Braxton-Miller supplied an average of 4,200 units of corrugated packaging stock per month to the Halden Ridge distribution center located in Fennimore, along with ancillary items such as strapping tape, pallet wrap, and moisture-control packets. Invoicing accuracy remained within acceptable tolerances throughout the period, with a discrepancy rate below the two percent threshold established in the original service level agreement.

During the renewal negotiation, representatives from both organizations met on three separate occasions to review pricing structures, delivery schedules, and quality assurance provisions. The initial meeting was held on January 9 and included Procurement Manager Dennis Ferraro on behalf of Halden Ridge and Account Executive Priya Nandakumar representing Braxton-Miller. Subsequent sessions on January 22 and February 3 addressed specific line-item adjustments, including a modest increase in per-unit pricing for packaging materials to reflect rising costs of raw cardboard stock, which the vendor attributed to broader market conditions affecting the paper products industry. Halden Ridge's Finance team, led by Controller Marguerite Solheim, reviewed the proposed pricing changes and determined that the adjustment, amounting to a 3.4 percent increase across the affected product categories, remained within budgetary parameters established for the upcoming fiscal year.

In addition to pricing, the renewed agreement incorporates several modifications to the original terms. The delivery window has been adjusted from a standard five-business-day turnaround to a four-business-day turnaround for standard orders, reflecting improvements in Braxton-Miller's regional distribution network following the opening of their new fulfillment facility in Cedarbrook. Rush order provisions remain unchanged, with a 48-hour expedited delivery option available at an additional surcharge of 12 percent above standard pricing. The parties also agreed to formalize a quarterly business review process, which had previously occurred on an informal basis, to ensure consistent communication regarding forecasted volume needs, seasonal demand fluctuations, and any emerging supply chain concerns that could affect service continuity.

The renewed contract also updates the insurance and liability provisions to align with Halden Ridge's revised vendor risk management policy, which was adopted company-wide following a broader compliance review conducted last year. Braxton-Miller has confirmed that its general liability coverage meets the updated minimum threshold of two million dollars per occurrence, and documentation verifying this coverage has been submitted to the Vendor Compliance office and filed accordingly. No changes were required to the indemnification clauses, as the existing language was found to satisfy current legal requirements upon review by outside counsel retained for this purpose.

Performance metrics from the prior term were factored into the renewal decision, with particular attention paid to the vendor scorecard maintained by the Operations department. Braxton-Miller achieved an overall performance rating of 4.2 out of 5 across the evaluated categories, which include on-time delivery, order accuracy, responsiveness to inquiries, and issue resolution timeliness. The lowest-scoring category was responsiveness to inquiries, where average response times to non-urgent requests occasionally exceeded the 24-hour benchmark outlined in the service agreement. Vendor Relations has requested that Braxton-Miller designate an additional point of contact to help address this gap, and the vendor has agreed to assign a secondary account representative, Colin Whitfield, who will support Ms. Nandakumar in managing day-to-day communications going forward.

Budgetary implications of the renewal were reviewed by the Finance department, and it was determined that the overall increase in projected spend, accounting for both the pricing adjustment and anticipated volume growth tied to the planned expansion of the Fennimore distribution center, falls within the range anticipated during the annual budget planning process. No additional budget approval beyond existing departmental authority was deemed necessary, though Finance recommended that spend against this contract be monitored on a quarterly basis alongside the newly implemented business review meetings.

Based on the findings summarized above, the Procurement Standards Committee recommends proceeding with the renewal under the terms outlined in this document. The finalized agreement is pending signature from both parties, with execution anticipated before the current contract's expiration date to avoid any lapse in service. A copy of the fully executed agreement, along with supporting documentation, will be retained in the vendor file maintained by the Procurement Standards Committee and made available for reference during future audit or review cycles. Any questions regarding this summary or the underlying negotiation process may be directed to the Vendor Relations office for clarification.

The Operations division, led by Regional Director Priya Anand, reported a modest improvement in throughput efficiency at the Danforth and Millbridge facilities, with average order-to-ship times decreasing from 14.3 hours to 12.9 hours over the course of the quarter. On the client services side, the Account Management team, under the direction of Marcus Feldwick, reported a client retention rate of 94.3 percent for the quarter, consistent with historical averages. Two accounts were lost during the period: the Corvale Logistics contract, which concluded as planned upon expiration of its original three-year term, and the smaller Thistlewood Imports account, which was discontinued at the client's request following an internal restructuring on their end unrelated to service performance. These losses were offset by the onboarding of two new mid-sized accounts, Bramford Textiles and Oakleigh Home Goods, both of which began shipping volume in September and are expected to reach full operational capacity by the end of the fourth quarter. Management has initiated preliminary discussions with Corestone regarding contract terms for the upcoming renewal period, with an eye toward negotiating more favorable fuel adjustment clauses. Looking ahead, management anticipates continued revenue growth in the fourth quarter driven by seasonal demand and the full ramp-up of the Bramford and Oakleigh accounts. Budget planning for fiscal year 2025 is underway, with department heads expected to submit preliminary projections by the end of October. SECTION 7: REMOTE WORK AND FLEXIBLE SCHEDULING POLICY

Meridian Falls Consulting Group ("the Company") recognizes that a balanced approach to work arrangements contributes to employee satisfaction and operational continuity. This policy establishes the framework under which employees may request remote work privileges or flexible scheduling arrangements, and it outlines the responsibilities of both the employee and the Company in maintaining productivity standards under such arrangements. This policy applies to all full-time and part-time employees who have completed their initial ninety-day probationary period, as determined by their respective department managers.

Eligibility for remote work arrangements is determined on a case-by-case basis and is subject to approval by the employee's direct supervisor and, where applicable, the Human Resources department. 1. Purpose and Scope

This document specifies the technical requirements, architectural framework, and implementation parameters for Phase II of the Meridian Records Management System, hereinafter referred to as MRMS. The purpose of this specification is to establish a shared understanding among stakeholders regarding system behavior, data handling procedures, integration touchpoints, and performance expectations prior to development commencement. This document supersedes the preliminary scoping memorandum issued on January 22, 2024, and incorporates revisions requested by the Northgate Municipal Services Division following the initial stakeholder review conducted on February 9, 2024.

The scope of Phase II encompasses the migration of legacy permit records from the Oakridge Archival Database into the MRMS platform, the establishment of a standardized intake workflow for new permit applications, and the integration of the system with the existing Northgate billing infrastructure managed by Halvorsen Utility Services. Phase II does not include public-facing web portal development, which is reserved for Phase III as outlined in the master project roadmap dated November 2023.

2. System Overview

MRMS is a modular records management platform designed to consolidate permit issuance, inspection scheduling, and compliance tracking functions previously distributed across three disconnected legacy systems. The core application is built on a three-tier architecture consisting of a presentation layer, an application logic layer, and a persistent data layer. The presentation layer will be accessible to internal Northgate staff through a desktop client and a limited mobile interface intended for field inspectors.

The application logic layer will be developed using a service-oriented approach, with discrete services handling permit intake, document management, scheduling, and audit logging. Each service will communicate through an internal messaging bus to reduce coupling between components and to facilitate future scalability. The persistent data layer will utilize a relational database managed by the vendor Pallister Data Systems, with nightly backups retained for a rolling ninety-day period in accordance with Northgate's records retention policy.

3. Functional Requirements

The intake workflow module shall allow authorized municipal staff to create, edit, and submit permit applications on behalf of external applicants. The system shall automatically generate a unique tracking number for each submitted application, formatted according to the existing Northgate convention of a two-letter department code followed by a six-digit sequential identifier.

The document management component shall support the upload and storage of attachments in common formats including PDF, TIFF, and JPEG, with a maximum individual file size of twenty-five megabytes. All uploaded documents shall be scanned for malformed file signatures prior to storage acceptance, and any file failing this validation shall be rejected with an explanatory message returned to the submitting user.

The scheduling module shall interface with the calendar system currently maintained by the Northgate Inspections Office to allow inspectors to view assigned site visits, mark inspections complete, and record findings directly within MRMS. Inspection records shall be linked to their corresponding permit application through the tracking number established at intake.

The audit logging service shall record all create, update, and delete operations performed within the system, capturing the user identifier, timestamp, and a description of the change made. Audit logs shall be immutable once written and shall be retained for a period no shorter than seven years, consistent with municipal recordkeeping requirements established by the Office of the City Clerk.

4. Integration Requirements

MRMS shall integrate with the Halvorsen Utility Services billing platform through a scheduled batch export process occurring at the close of business each weekday. This export shall transmit newly finalized permit fee assessments in a fixed-width text format specified in Appendix C of this document. Reconciliation reports confirming successful transmission shall be generated automatically and stored within the document management component for reference by the Northgate Finance Office.

Migration of legacy records from the Oakridge Archival Database shall occur in three sequential batches, each corresponding to a distinct permit category grouping as agreed upon during the February stakeholder review. A dedicated migration utility, developed by Callahan Ferris Systems Group specifically for this engagement, shall handle field mapping, data normalization, and duplicate detection. Any records flagged as duplicates or containing incomplete mandatory fields shall be routed to a manual review queue for resolution by Northgate records staff prior to final import.

5. Performance and Availability Requirements

The system shall be designed to support a minimum of one hundred fifty concurrent users during standard business hours without degradation of response times beyond two seconds for standard query operations. Scheduled maintenance windows shall be limited to Sunday mornings between the hours of one and five, and advance notice of no less than seventy-two hours shall be provided to all internal users prior to any planned outage.

System availability outside of scheduled maintenance windows shall meet or exceed 99.5 percent, measured on a monthly basis. Any unplanned outage exceeding thirty minutes shall trigger an incident report to be delivered to the Northgate Information Technology Office within one business day of resolution.

Initial Contact — March 4, 10:12 AM
Customer contact Diane Ostrowski of Meridian Office Supply Co. submitted a ticket via the online support portal regarding recurring discrepancies in monthly invoice totals generated by the InvoiceTrack Pro software, version 6.3.1. Ms. Ostrowski indicated that for the past three billing cycles, the automatically generated subtotal on invoices exceeding fifty line items did not match the sum of the individual line items when recalculated manually in a spreadsheet. She noted the discrepancy was small, typically between $0.01 and $0.14, but that her accounting department flagged it during month-end reconciliation and requested clarification before closing the books. Ms. Ostrowski attached three sample invoices (Invoice #10432, #10458, #10471) demonstrating the issue and requested a callback or email response within two business days per the terms of her support contract tier.

First Response — March 4, 2:47 PM
Representative Colin Vasquez reviewed the submitted invoices and confirmed the discrepancies as described. Mr. Vasquez noted that the pattern appeared consistent with a known rounding behavior in the tax calculation module when line items are grouped across multiple tax jurisdictions within a single invoice. He requested additional information from Ms. Ostrowski, specifically whether the affected invoices involved customers located in more than one state, as this would help confirm the hypothesis. He also asked whether the discrepancy occurred only on invoices generated after the January 15 software update or if it predated that release.

Customer Follow-Up — March 5, 9:03 AM
Ms. Ostrowski replied confirming that all three sample invoices involved shipments to customers in both Ohio and Pennsylvania, and that the discrepancy did not appear in any invoices prior to the January update. She stated that her department had not changed any internal settings around that time and asked whether a rollback of the update was feasible while a permanent fix was developed. She also asked whether other customers had reported the same issue, as she wanted to understand whether this was isolated to her account configuration.

Internal Escalation Note — March 5, 11:20 AM
Mr. Vasquez escalated the ticket internally to the Billing Systems Engineering team (assigned to engineer Priya Ramanathan) with a summary of the reported behavior, the version number, and the two sample invoices most clearly demonstrating the rounding inconsistency. He flagged the ticket as related to a broader pattern observed in four other accounts since the January 15 release, referencing internal tracking ticket ENG-5502 for cross-reference. He recommended against a full rollback given that the update also contained a security patch for the login authentication module, and instead requested an expedited patch timeline.

Engineering Response — March 6, 4:15 PM
Ms. Ramanathan confirmed that the rounding issue stemmed from a change in how the tax engine aggregates line-item tax before rounding, rather than rounding each line item individually before summing. She indicated that a corrective patch, version 6.3.2, was already in testing and expected to be released within five business days. In the interim, she suggested a manual workaround: generating a supplementary reconciliation report through the "Export Detailed Tax Breakdown" feature under Reports > Tax Summary, which calculates totals using the pre-aggregation method and would match manual spreadsheet totals. Mr. Vasquez was asked to relay this workaround to the customer along with an estimated timeline for the permanent fix.

Customer Communication — March 6, 5:32 PM
Mr. Vasquez emailed Ms. Ostrowski with the explanation of the rounding behavior, instructions for generating the supplementary tax breakdown report as a temporary workaround, and confirmation that a patch was expected the following week. He also clarified that the discrepancy did not affect the actual amounts charged to end customers, only the internal reconciliation totals, since the invoice PDFs themselves reflected correct final amounts. He offered to schedule a brief phone call to walk through the workaround if needed.

Customer Follow-Up — March 7, 8:41 AM
Ms. Ostrowski responded that she had tested the workaround on Invoice #10471 and confirmed the totals now matched her manual spreadsheet calculations. She thanked Mr. Vasquez for the clear explanation and stated a phone call was not necessary. She asked to be notified once version 6.3.2 was released so her team could resume using the standard report format without the extra export step.

Patch Release Notification — March 12, 9:00 AM
Mr. Vasquez sent a follow-up email confirming that version 6.3.2 had been released overnight and included the corrected tax aggregation logic. He provided a brief summary of the update changelog and noted that the update would apply automatically for accounts on the standard maintenance plan, which included Meridian Office Supply Co. He asked Ms. Ostrowski to run one test invoice after the update applied and confirm the totals matched expected values, purely as a precaution before closing the ticket.

### 1. Purpose and Scope

This document defines the technical requirements, architecture, and implementation parameters for the Meridian Ledger Reconciliation Module, version 2.3 (hereafter "MLRM" or "the Module"). The Module is designed to automate the reconciliation of transactional records between the Corvid Analytics Solutions internal general ledger system, known internally as Halden Ledger Suite, and third-party vendor invoicing platforms utilized by regional distribution partners. This specification is intended for use by the Development Team, Quality Assurance personnel, and integration partners who require a comprehensive understanding of the Module's functional boundaries, data handling procedures, and interface requirements. This document does not cover deployment scheduling, licensing terms, or personnel training materials, which are addressed under separate documentation issued by the Program Management Office.

### 2. Background

The Meridian Ledger Reconciliation Module was commissioned following an internal audit conducted in the third quarter of the prior fiscal year, which identified recurring discrepancies between reported vendor invoices and recorded disbursements within three regional offices, namely the Brindlewood, Fenmark, and Castellane branches. The audit, led by Internal Controls Director Margaret Oswin, recommended the development of an automated reconciliation tool to reduce manual reconciliation labor and to minimize the incidence of unmatched or duplicate entries. This specification builds upon the findings documented in Audit Report AR-2023-119 and incorporates feedback gathered during stakeholder interviews conducted with regional finance leads Thomas Everley and Priya Ramanathan.

### 3. System Overview

MLRM operates as a middleware component situated between the Halden Ledger Suite database and external vendor data feeds. The Module ingests transaction records in comma-separated value format, XML format, or via direct API calls where supported by the vendor platform. Upon ingestion, records are normalized into a standardized internal schema referred to as the Unified Transaction Record (UTR). The UTR format includes fields for transaction identifier, vendor identifier, transaction date, amount, currency code, and a reconciliation status flag. Once normalized, records are passed through the Matching Engine, which applies a series of configurable rules to identify corresponding entries between the internal ledger and the external vendor feed.

The Matching Engine supports both exact-match and fuzzy-match reconciliation modes. Exact-match mode requires identical values across transaction identifier, amount, and date fields. Fuzzy-match mode, intended for use where vendor systems introduce minor formatting inconsistencies, applies configurable tolerance thresholds for date variance (default setting of plus or minus two business days) and amount variance (default setting of plus or minus one percent). Records that fail to match under either mode are routed to the Exception Queue for manual review by designated reconciliation analysts.

### 4. Functional Requirements

The Module shall support batch processing of transaction volumes up to two hundred fifty thousand records per reconciliation cycle without degradation of processing time beyond the established service level target of four hours per cycle. The Module shall maintain a complete audit trail of all matching decisions, including timestamps, applied rule sets, and the identity of any analyst who manually overrides an automated match determination. All audit trail data shall be retained for a minimum period of seven years in accordance with corporate records retention policy RP-4402.

The Module shall provide a configuration interface allowing authorized administrators to adjust matching tolerance thresholds without requiring a code deployment. This interface shall be accessible only to users holding the Reconciliation Administrator role within the Corvid Analytics Solutions identity management system, and all configuration changes shall be logged with the administrator's user identifier and the timestamp of the change.

The Module shall generate a daily summary report detailing the total number of records processed, the number of successful matches under exact-match mode, the number of successful matches under fuzzy-match mode, and the number of records routed to the Exception Queue. This report shall be distributed automatically via internal email to the distribution list maintained by the Finance Operations team, with Derek Halloway serving as the current list owner.

### 5. Non-Functional Requirements

The Module shall be deployed within the existing Corvid Analytics Solutions data center infrastructure and shall not require provisioning of additional physical hardware beyond the two application servers already allocated under infrastructure ticket INF-8834. The Module shall maintain an uptime target of 99.5 percent measured on a monthly basis, excluding scheduled maintenance windows communicated at least seventy-two hours in advance.

Data at rest within the Module's staging database shall be encrypted using AES-256 encryption, consistent with corporate data security policy DS-1120. Data in transit between the Module and vendor platforms shall be secured using TLS 1.2 or higher. Access to the Module's administrative functions shall require multi-factor authentication in accordance with existing corporate access control standards.

### 6. Interfaces

The Module interfaces with the Halden Ledger Suite via a dedicated read-write database connection managed through the existing Enterprise Service Bus, maintained by the Infrastructure Services group under the direction of Networking Lead Samuel Bricktoft. External vendor interfaces vary by partner and are documented individually in Appendix C of the associated integration guide, maintained separately from this specification. Any changes to vendor-side data formats shall be communicated to the Development Team no fewer than fourteen calendar days prior to implementation to allow for adequate testing.

Prepared by the Site Reliability Engineering team at Meridian Cloud Solutions, this report documents the investigation into the service disruption affecting the Halyard Billing Platform on the morning of March 14th. The incident was assigned tracking number INC-20440 and was classified as a Severity 2 event due to its impact on customer-facing invoice generation and payment reconciliation processes. This document summarizes the timeline, root cause analysis, business impact, and remediation steps agreed upon by the engineering and product stakeholders involved.

At approximately 6:42 AM Central Time, automated monitoring alerts from the Overwatch dashboard flagged elevated error rates on the invoice-generation microservice, which is maintained by the Payments Infrastructure team under the direction of engineering manager Priya Nandakumar. The alerts indicated a spike in HTTP 500 responses originating from the InvoiceCompositor service, a component responsible for aggregating usage records from the Metering Service and applying customer-specific pricing rules before generating final invoices. Within eleven minutes, on-call engineer Marcus Delgado acknowledged the page and began initial triage, confirming that the error rate had climbed from a baseline of 0.3 percent to over 22 percent across the affected region.

Marcus's initial investigation pointed to a recent deployment that had gone out the previous evening as part of release cycle 4.18.2, which introduced a caching layer intended to reduce load on the downstream pricing rules engine, internally known as TariffEngine. The caching layer had been developed by the Pricing Platform team, led by Devon Osei, and had passed all automated regression tests in the staging environment prior to release. However, staging traffic patterns did not closely mirror production traffic during month-end billing cycles, when a much higher volume of invoice regeneration requests occurs due to customer plan changes and retroactive credits.

As a courtesy, we've kept this name active, but it just redirects behind the scenes to "verified_output_channel" — that's the one doing the real processing.

By 7:15 AM, Marcus escalated the incident to a full incident bridge, pulling in additional engineers from the Payments Infrastructure and Pricing Platform teams, along with a representative from Customer Success, Elena Vasquez, who began fielding inbound reports from enterprise clients experiencing delayed or malformed invoices. Elena's team had already logged fourteen support tickets from customers in the logistics and manufacturing verticals, several of whom rely on same-day invoice delivery for their own downstream accounting processes. This customer impact elevated the urgency of the investigation and prompted the incident commander, Rajiv Patel, to formally declare the event a Severity 2 incident at 7:23 AM, triggering the standard communication protocol to affected account managers.

The root cause was identified at approximately 8:05 AM. The newly introduced caching layer within TariffEngine had a subtle bug in its cache invalidation logic. When a customer's pricing tier was updated mid-cycle, the cache was not properly invalidated for previously computed line items, resulting in stale pricing data being applied to new invoice line items generated after the tier change. In cases where the mismatch between cached and current data exceeded a validation threshold built into the InvoiceCompositor's consistency checker, the service would throw an exception rather than silently proceed, which explained the surge in 500 errors rather than a silent data corruption issue. While the fail-safe behavior prevented incorrect invoices from being sent to customers, it did so at the cost of availability, effectively blocking invoice generation entirely for any customer who had undergone a plan change within the caching window.

Once the root cause was confirmed, the team made the decision to roll back the 4.18.2 release rather than attempt a forward fix under time pressure, given the complexity of the caching logic and the desire to restore service as quickly as possible. The rollback was initiated at 8:19 AM and completed by 8:47 AM, after which error rates began declining steadily. By 9:15 AM, error rates had returned to baseline levels, and the incident bridge began transitioning into recovery verification. Marcus and a colleague from the Data Integrity team, Wen Sato, spent the following two hours manually auditing invoices generated during the incident window to identify any that may have been affected by the stale pricing bug but had not triggered the consistency checker's exception threshold. This audit identified sixty-three invoices requiring correction, all of which were reissued to affected customers by end of day with an accompanying explanatory note drafted by the Customer Success team.

The retrospective meeting was held on March 17th and included representatives from Payments Infrastructure, Pricing Platform, Customer Success, and Quality Assurance. The group agreed that the staging environment's traffic simulation needed to be updated to better reflect month-end billing patterns, particularly the volume and timing of mid-cycle plan changes, which had not been adequately represented in the pre-release testing suite. Devon Osei's team committed to rewriting the cache invalidation logic with more granular tracking of pricing tier changes, alongside a broader unit test suite specifically targeting edge cases around mid-cycle updates. Additionally, the group recommended that future releases touching the TariffEngine or InvoiceCompositor components include a mandatory canary deployment phase, during which a small percentage of production traffic would be routed through the new code path before a full rollout, allowing issues to surface with limited customer impact.

Action items from the retrospective were assigned owners and target completion dates, with the staging traffic simulation update assigned to the Quality Assurance team with a deadline of April 4th, and the cache invalidation rewrite assigned to the Pricing Platform team with a deadline of April 18th. Rajiv Patel will follow up with both teams during the next engineering sync to confirm progress, and a summary of this incident will be shared with the broader engineering organization as part of the monthly reliability review.

Quarterly Business Performance Report
Third Quarter, Fiscal Year 2024
Prepared by the Office of Corporate Planning, Meridian Fenwick Holdings

Executive Summary

This report presents an overview of operational and financial performance for Meridian Fenwick Holdings during the third quarter of fiscal year 2024, covering the period from July 1 through September 30. The quarter was characterized by steady demand across core business lines, moderate cost pressures related to logistics, and continued progress on the enterprise resource planning migration initiated in the previous fiscal year. Overall revenue for the quarter reached $48.2 million, representing a 3.4 percent increase over the prior quarter and a 6.1 percent increase over the same period last year. Operating margin held at 14.7 percent, consistent with internal targets set during the annual planning cycle. This report summarizes performance by division, reviews progress against strategic initiatives, and outlines areas requiring continued management attention heading into the fourth quarter.

Divisional Performance

The Industrial Products Division, led by Regional Director Colin Aspenwall, reported revenue of $21.6 million for the quarter, a 2.9 percent increase from the prior period. Growth was primarily attributed to sustained order volume from long-standing clients in the manufacturing sector, particularly in the Midwest and Southeast regions. Mr. Aspenwall's team noted a modest uptick in raw material costs, which was partially offset by renegotiated freight contracts finalized in August. The division's backlog remains healthy, with confirmed orders extending through the first half of the next fiscal year.

The Consumer Solutions Division, under the direction of Priya Ramanathan, posted revenue of $16.8 million, up 4.5 percent from the second quarter. This growth was driven largely by the successful rollout of the updated product line introduced in June, which exceeded initial sales projections by approximately 8 percent. Ms. Ramanathan's team continues to monitor inventory turnover closely, as warehouse capacity constraints in the Northeast distribution center have created minor delays in order fulfillment. Plans to expand warehouse capacity are currently under review by the facilities committee and are expected to be finalized before the end of the calendar year.

The Professional Services Division, managed by Terrence Okafor, recorded revenue of $9.8 million, representing a slight decline of 1.2 percent from the prior quarter. This decrease was primarily attributed to the completion of two large consulting engagements in July, with replacement contracts not yet fully ramped. Mr. Okafor indicated that the sales pipeline for the fourth quarter remains robust, with three new engagements scheduled to begin in October, which should offset the current shortfall in the coming period.

Financial Overview

Gross profit for the quarter totaled $19.3 million, reflecting a gross margin of 40.0 percent, a slight improvement from 39.1 percent in the previous quarter. Selling, general, and administrative expenses were $9.6 million, representing 19.9 percent of revenue, consistent with historical averages. Research and development spending remained stable at $2.1 million, primarily allocated to the Consumer Solutions Division's ongoing product refinement efforts and to preliminary feasibility studies for a potential new product category under evaluation by the innovation team.

Cash flow from operations for the quarter was $6.4 million, supporting continued investment in capital expenditures, which totaled $3.2 million. These expenditures were directed primarily toward equipment upgrades at the Industrial Products Division's primary manufacturing facility and continued investment in the enterprise resource planning system migration. The company's cash and cash equivalents balance at quarter end stood at $22.7 million, providing adequate liquidity to support planned initiatives through the remainder of the fiscal year.

Strategic Initiatives Update

The enterprise resource planning migration, overseen by Chief Information Officer Naomi Castellano, remains on schedule, with the finance and procurement modules now fully operational across all divisions. The human resources and inventory management modules are scheduled for rollout in the fourth quarter, with training sessions for affected staff currently being coordinated by the change management team. Third Quarter, Fiscal Year 2024
Prepared by the Office of Corporate Planning
Meridian Fold Industries, Inc.

Executive Summary

This report provides a summary review of operational and financial performance for Meridian Fold Industries, Inc. for the third quarter of fiscal year 2024, covering the period of July 1 through September 30. Overall performance during the quarter reflected continued stabilization following the supply chain disruptions noted in the previous two reporting periods. Revenue across the organization increased modestly compared to the second quarter, while operating expenses remained largely consistent with prior forecasts. The following sections address performance by division, along with commentary on staffing, procurement, and administrative matters that were relevant to the quarter under review.

Divisional Performance

The Packaging Solutions Division, under the continued direction of Regional Manager Harold Denby, reported a 4.2 percent increase in net revenue relative to the second quarter. This growth was attributed primarily to renewed contract volume from three long-standing clients in the food service sector, as well as the onboarding of two new mid-sized accounts in the industrial goods sector. Mr. Denby's team noted that production throughput at the Wexford facility improved following the resolution of a minor equipment calibration issue that had affected output in early July. No significant safety incidents were recorded during the quarter, and the facility maintained its consecutive streak of 214 days without a reportable workplace injury.

The Distribution and Logistics Division, led by Senior Manager Priya Chandrasekaran, experienced a more modest quarter, with revenue essentially flat relative to the prior period, reflecting a 0.6 percent increase. Fuel costs remained elevated relative to the same quarter last year, which continued to compress margins within the freight brokerage segment. Ms. Chandrasekaran's team implemented a revised route optimization protocol in August, and early indications suggest this adjustment may yield modest cost savings beginning in the fourth quarter. The division also completed a routine audit of its vehicle maintenance records, which identified no material deficiencies requiring escalation.

The Client Services Division, overseen by Director Wendell Pruitt, reported steady performance consistent with internal projections. Customer retention rates held at 91.3 percent, a figure that has remained stable across the last four consecutive quarters. Mr. Pruitt's team fielded a total of 1,842 service inquiries during the quarter, a slight increase from the 1,790 inquiries recorded in the second quarter, which staff attributed to seasonal demand patterns rather than any underlying service issue. Average response time to client inquiries improved marginally, from 6.4 hours to 5.9 hours, following the redistribution of intake responsibilities among the customer service team.

The Administrative and Finance Division, managed by Controller Marguerite Solheim, completed its scheduled internal review of expense reporting procedures during the quarter. This review did not identify any significant irregularities. Ms. Solheim's office also finalized preparations for the upcoming external audit, which is scheduled to commence in the fourth quarter and will be conducted by the firm of Castellane and Byrne, LLP, consistent with prior engagements.

Human Resources and Staffing

Total headcount across the organization increased slightly during the quarter, from 486 employees at the close of the second quarter to 493 employees at the close of the third quarter. This net increase reflects the hiring of eleven new employees across the Packaging Solutions and Client Services divisions, offset by four voluntary departures. Human Resources Director Colin Aspenwall reported that the organization's voluntary turnover rate for the quarter was 2.1 percent, consistent with historical averages for this time of year. The department also completed its annual review of the employee benefits package, and no substantive changes are anticipated for the upcoming enrollment period.

Training and development activities continued as scheduled, with 68 employees completing the company's standard onboarding curriculum and an additional 42 employees completing supplemental compliance training related to updated workplace safety guidelines. Mr. Aspenwall's office noted that participation rates in the optional professional development program remained consistent with prior quarters, at approximately 27 percent of eligible staff.

Procurement and Vendor Relations

The Procurement Office, under the direction of Senior Buyer Lucille Farraday, renewed contracts with two of the company's principal raw material suppliers during the quarter, both under terms consistent with the prior agreements. Ms. Farraday's office also conducted a routine vendor performance review, which confirmed satisfactory delivery timelines and quality metrics across all major suppliers. No new vendor relationships were established during this period, and no existing relationships were terminated.

Facilities and Capital Projects

The ongoing renovation of the Dunmore Street administrative offices, which began in the second quarter, remained on schedule and within the originally approved budget. Facilities Manager Terrence Okafor reported that the project is expected to reach substantial completion by the end of the fourth quarter, with final inspection anticipated in early January. No additional capital expenditure requests were submitted during the quarter beyond those previously approved by the Board.

Outlook

Management anticipates continued modest growth into the fourth quarter, supported by seasonal demand within the Packaging Solutions Division and the anticipated benefits of the logistics route optimization initiative. The organization does not currently anticipate any material changes to its operating structure, staffing levels, or strategic priorities in the near term. This report will be followed by the standard fourth-quarter and annual summary reports, to be distributed according to the established reporting calendar.

Under the renewed agreement, the base licensing fee will increase from $184,500 annually to $198,750 annually, representing an increase of approximately 7.7 percent. This adjustment was attributed by Corvale's account representative, Priya Anand, to increased infrastructure costs and the inclusion of two additional software modules that were previously billed separately: the predictive inventory forecasting tool and the expanded reporting dashboard suite. Finance department analysis, conducted by Senior Analyst Devon Ruiz, confirmed that bundling these modules into the base fee results in a net cost reduction of roughly $6,200 annually compared to maintaining them as standalone add-ons under the previous fee structure. This finding was a significant factor in the Procurement Committee's recommendation to proceed with renewal rather than pursue alternative vendors during this cycle.

The renewed agreement also introduces several changes to the service level commitments outlined in Schedule C of the original contract. Notably, the guaranteed response time for critical system outages has been reduced from four hours to two hours, with Corvale agreeing to maintain a dedicated on-call technician assigned specifically to Halden Ridge Logistics Corporation's account during standard business hours. Non-critical support requests will continue to follow the existing 24-hour response window. In addition, the renewed contract stipulates that Corvale will conduct quarterly system performance reviews with Halden Ridge's IT department, a practice that was previously conducted on an ad hoc basis and was cited by IT Manager Sonia Whitfield as an area needing more consistent structure.

Legal review of the renewal was completed by outside counsel at Prescott and Lane LLP, with particular attention given to the data handling and liability provisions given the expanded scope of services related to the new forecasting module, which will process historical shipment data across all three distribution centers. Counsel confirmed that the updated data processing addendum aligns with the company's existing data governance policy and does not introduce any material changes to liability exposure. The termination clause remains largely unchanged from the prior agreement, allowing either party to terminate the contract with 90 days written notice, though the renewed version clarifies that any pro-rated refund calculations will be based on the most recent quarterly invoice rather than the annual total, a change requested by Finance to simplify reconciliation in the event of early termination.

Training and onboarding support for the two new software modules will be provided at no additional cost during the first 60 days following the renewal's effective date, per an accommodation negotiated by Procurement Lead Harold Denby. This includes two on-site training sessions at Danforth Crossing and one remote training session for staff at Millbrook Junction and Ashcombe Terminal. Feedback from department heads at both facilities indicated a preference for in-person training where feasible, and Corvale has agreed to evaluate the possibility of an additional on-site session at Ashcombe Terminal pending scheduling availability in the coming weeks.

The Procurement Committee's overall assessment of the renewal is favorable, citing the vendor's consistent performance record, the cost efficiencies achieved through module bundling, and the improved service level commitments as sufficient justification for continuing the relationship without initiating a formal request for proposal process. It was noted, however, that the committee will revisit this decision at the next renewal cycle and may consider soliciting competitive bids at that time, particularly if service performance metrics decline or if comparable vendors demonstrate materially lower pricing during that period. A follow-up review of Corvale's performance against the updated service level commitments is scheduled for the midpoint of the new contract term, with results to be reported back to the committee no later than April of next year.

This summary has been circulated to relevant department heads for informational purposes and does not supersede the fully executed contract document, which remains on file with the Legal department and is available upon request for detailed reference regarding specific contractual language, payment schedules, and appendices.

Prepared for the Executive Leadership Team of Halden & Marsh Consolidated Industries, this report summarizes operational and financial performance for the third quarter of the fiscal year, covering the period of July 1 through September 30. The information contained herein was compiled by the Office of Corporate Planning under the direction of Regional Operations Director Colin Aldrich, with contributions from the Finance, Logistics, and Human Resources departments. This document is intended for internal distribution only and should be reviewed alongside the supplementary spreadsheets circulated separately by the Finance team.

Overall, the quarter was characterized by steady, if unspectacular, performance across most business units. Consolidated revenue for the quarter reached approximately 14.2 million dollars, representing a 2.6 percent increase over the previous quarter and a 4.1 percent increase over the same period last year. This growth was driven primarily by continued momentum in the Northfield Distribution Division, which benefited from the completion of the Ashworth Logistics Upgrade Project earlier in the spring. That project, which involved the replacement of aging conveyor systems at the Millbrook Distribution Center, appears to have reduced average order fulfillment times by roughly eleven percent, a change that has translated into modest but measurable improvements in customer retention metrics tracked by the Client Services team.

The Manufacturing Division, led by Plant Operations Manager Denise Okafor, reported production output broadly in line with targets set during the spring planning cycle. Unit output at the Carrowgate facility increased slightly, from 218,400 units in the second quarter to 221,750 units in the third, while the Bellmont facility experienced a minor dip attributed to scheduled maintenance downtime during the first two weeks of August. This downtime had been anticipated in the annual maintenance calendar and did not materially affect the division's ability to meet outstanding customer orders. Raw material costs remained relatively stable during the quarter, though the Procurement team noted a slight uptick in freight surcharges associated with imported polymer components, a trend that is being monitored closely given ongoing volatility in shipping markets.

On the sales and business development front, the Client Accounts group, under the supervision of Senior Account Manager Priya Ramanathan, closed fourteen new contracts during the quarter, six of which fall under the mid-market segment and eight under the enterprise segment. Notable among these was the renewal and expansion of the service agreement with Thornfield Regional Retailers, a longstanding client whose contract now includes an additional distribution lane connecting the Southbridge warehouse to their newly opened retail locations in the tri-county area. The sales pipeline for the fourth quarter appears healthy, with approximately 3.4 million dollars in prospective contract value currently under active negotiation, though it should be noted that historical conversion rates suggest that not all of this figure will materialize into signed agreements.

Human Resources reported a relatively stable quarter with respect to staffing levels. Total headcount across all divisions stood at 1,042 employees as of September 30, a modest increase from 1,021 at the close of the previous quarter. This growth is largely attributable to the onboarding of new warehouse associates at the Southbridge facility in anticipation of increased seasonal volume expected in the fourth quarter. Voluntary turnover remained within the range considered normal for the industry, at approximately 3.8 percent for the quarter, though the Talent Retention Committee, chaired by HR Director Marcus Whitfield, has continued its review of exit interview data to identify any emerging patterns that might warrant further attention heading into the next fiscal year.

The Finance Department, under the direction of Controller Elena Vasquez, reported that operating expenses remained within budgeted parameters for the quarter, with total operating costs at approximately 11.6 million dollars. This figure includes routine expenditures related to facilities maintenance, utilities, insurance premiums, and administrative overhead. Gross margin for the quarter came in at 18.3 percent, a slight improvement over the 17.9 percent recorded in the prior quarter, attributable in part to the fulfillment efficiencies described earlier as well as modest reductions in per-unit shipping costs negotiated with the company's primary freight carrier, Redwing Transport Solutions. The Finance team has flagged the upcoming renewal of the company's general liability insurance policy, scheduled for early in the fourth quarter, as an item requiring attention from senior leadership given anticipated premium increases across the industry.

**Meridian Fowler & Associates, LLC**

This section establishes the standards and procedures governing employee travel undertaken on behalf of Meridian Fowler & Associates, LLC (hereinafter referred to as "the Company"), as well as the corresponding procedures for the submission, review, and reimbursement of business-related expenses. All employees who incur travel or incidental expenses in the course of performing their assigned duties are expected to comply fully with the provisions outlined below. Failure to adhere to these guidelines may result in delayed reimbursement or, in cases of repeated noncompliance, disciplinary review in accordance with Section 12 of this handbook.

All business travel must be authorized in advance by the employee's direct supervisor or department head. Authorization should be obtained no later than five business days prior to the anticipated date of departure, except in circumstances involving urgent client engagements or unforeseen operational needs, in which case retroactive approval may be granted at the discretion of the supervising manager. For example, when Regional Sales Director Colin Marsh was asked to attend an emergency client meeting in Dayton with less than twenty-four hours' notice, his manager, Patricia Onwuegbuzie, granted expedited approval through the Company's internal travel authorization portal, and the trip was documented retroactively within the standard reporting window. Employees are encouraged to consult with their supervisors regarding the most cost-effective means of travel, taking into account scheduling constraints, client expectations, and overall project budgets.

Reimbursable expenses generally include transportation costs such as airfare, rail fare, or mileage for personal vehicle use; lodging expenses for overnight stays required by the itinerary; reasonable meal expenses incurred during travel; and incidental costs directly related to the business purpose of the trip, including parking fees, tolls, and necessary communication charges. Airfare should be booked in economy class unless travel time exceeds six hours, in which case premium economy may be approved by a department vice president. Lodging accommodations should be selected with reasonable regard for cost, proximity to the business destination, and safety. The Company maintains preferred vendor relationships with several national hotel chains, and employees are encouraged, though not required, to utilize these vendors when available, as doing so may result in reduced rates and simplified billing procedures for the Company.

Meal expenses incurred while traveling are subject to a daily per diem cap, which is reviewed annually by the Finance Department and communicated to all staff through the internal policy bulletin. As of the most recent review, the per diem for domestic travel is set at sixty-five dollars per day, inclusive of gratuities, and the per diem for international travel is adjusted according to destination-specific cost-of-living indices maintained by the Finance Department. Employees are not required to submit itemized meal receipts when claiming the standard per diem; however, any request for reimbursement exceeding the established cap must be accompanied by an itemized receipt and a brief written justification, to be reviewed by the employee's supervisor prior to submission to Finance.

All expense reports must be submitted through the Company's designated expense management system within fourteen calendar days of the completion of travel. Reports submitted after this period may be subject to delayed processing or, in cases exceeding thirty days without prior notice to Finance, may be denied outright. Each report must include original or digitally scanned receipts for all expenses exceeding twenty-five dollars, a clear statement of business purpose, and the names of any additional attendees if the expense pertains to a client meal or entertainment function. For instance, when Associate Consultant Marisol Petrenko submitted a reimbursement request for a client dinner in Chicago, she was required to list the names of the three client representatives in attendance, along with a brief note describing the nature of the discussion, in accordance with the documentation standards described herein.

Expenses that are personal in nature, including but not limited to entertainment unrelated to business purposes, spa services, personal grooming, traffic citations, or expenses incurred for the benefit of family members or non-employee companions accompanying the traveler, are not eligible for reimbursement under any circumstance. Employees who are uncertain whether a particular expense qualifies for reimbursement are encouraged to consult with their supervisor or with a member of the Finance Department prior to incurring the expense, rather than after the fact, in order to avoid unnecessary delays or disputes during the review process.

Reimbursement payments are typically processed within ten business days of an approved expense report being received by the Finance Department, and payments are issued through the same method as the employee's regular payroll disbursement. Employees who believe an error has occurred in the processing of their reimbursement should contact the Finance Department directly, providing their expense report reference number, and allow a minimum of five business days for the matter to be reviewed and resolved.

The Company reserves the right to periodically audit expense reports and supporting documentation to ensure compliance with this policy and with applicable tax regulations. Employees selected for audit will be notified in writing and asked to provide any additional documentation necessary to substantiate the expenses in question. Section 7: Remote Work and Flexible Scheduling Policy

Meridian Fenwick Logistics Group ("the Company") recognizes that the nature of contemporary work has evolved considerably since the founding of our organization, and that many roles across our departments can be performed effectively outside of a traditional office environment. This section outlines the Company's expectations, procedures, and eligibility requirements for employees who wish to participate in remote work arrangements, whether on a full-time, hybrid, or occasional basis. This policy applies to all full-time and part-time employees who have completed their initial ninety-day probationary period, unless otherwise specified in an individual employment agreement or departmental exception approved by Human Resources.

Eligibility for remote work is determined primarily by job function and departmental need rather than tenure alone. Employees in roles that require regular in-person interaction with warehouse operations, such as those assigned to the Dornbridge Distribution Center or the Halvern Regional Fulfillment Hub, are generally not eligible for remote arrangements, given the physical nature of their responsibilities. Conversely, employees in administrative, analytical, customer support, and project coordination roles, including staff working on the Company's ongoing Meridian Connect supply chain visibility initiative, may be considered for hybrid or fully remote schedules upon manager approval. Requests for remote work must be submitted in writing to the employee's direct supervisor using the Remote Work Request Form available on the internal portal, and supervisors are expected to respond within ten business days.
